src.label: Ministry of Agriculture (MAG) / SENASA — sanitary requirements for importing dogs and cats

head: A vet exam within two weeks, an official health certificate, microchip and vaccines are all required.
lines: SENASA requires a clinical exam by a vet in the country of origin within the two weeks before travel, and an official health certificate from that country's health authority. A microchip number must be written on the certificate, and rabies vaccination is required for animals over three months old.

Dogs also need vaccines against distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus and leptospirosis, and cats against feline rhinotracheitis, calicivirus and panleukopenia. Dates, brand, lot number and validity of each vaccine go on the certificate and must still be valid at entry.

Internal and external deworming must be given within 15 days before arrival, with brand and lot recorded. A pet declared as cargo also needs a prior import permit arranged through a customs agency. If requirements are not met, entry is denied and the pet is returned to its country of origin.
